To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nonlinear power spectrum of clustering quintessence models can be significantly different from that of the ΛCDM model, depending on the value assumed by the speed of sound of the quintessence field, and that the relation between the linear and nonlinear growth function should be taken into account when constraining models with a clustering quintessence.

in clustering quintessency cosmologies: the linear growth function is significantly different from the one in smooth quintessency models, and the difference increases with the sound speed; the nonlinear corrections to the density power spectrum are small but not negligible, and the corrections are smaller the smaller the speed of sound.
the nonlinear evolution of perturbations is affected by the speed of sound of dark energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nonlinear evolution of perturbations in quintessence models with inhomogeneities, in particular with a vanishing sound speed.
the nonlinear evolution of perturbations in clustering dark energy scenarios.
the nonlinear evolution of the total density power spectrum for a class of models where the dark energy is inhomogeneous and clustering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlinear power spectrum is a very good probe of the dark energy equation of state, but only when the dark energy is smooth and not clustering.
the nonlinear evolution of structures can be used to distinguish between smooth and clustered dark energy models, but not to discriminate among the different clustered models.
the nonlinear power spectrum is a more sensitive observable for constraining the nature of dark energy than the linear growth of structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
clustering quintessence models are not as simple as smooth quintessence ones.
the nonlinear evolution is not sensitive to the inhomogeneous nature of the dark energy component.

the nonlinear evolution of the density perturbation in clustering quintesscence cosmology can be described by a single equation, but the evolution is not the same as that for the smooth quintessence model with the same equation of states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clustering of dark energy perturbations can significantly affect the nonlinear power spectrum and should not be ignored.
the nonlinear evolution in quintessence models is not a mere rescaling of the ΛCDM one.
, in clustering quintessences, the nonlinear power spectrum is not a good discriminator between models, since the nonlinear corrections are small.
